title: Stone Pine: Ancient Umbrella Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: The flat-topped pine that gives the Mediterranean its skyline, normally wider than it is tall. Eight mapped, from Setubal to Istanbul.
intro: The stone pine is the tree that gives the Mediterranean skyline its flat topped silhouette, and it normally does that from a bare trunk ten or fifteen metres up, spreading wider than it grows tall. The one on Florence's Bobolino hillside ignores the rule and stands 31.5 metres. Two on a Setubal street are older than the street, left over from woodland the city expanded across, which is why they stand in no pattern at all. Istanbul's Ata Fistik Cami gave a whole hill its name and was brought there from the Aegean rather than growing there naturally. Naples has the odd one out: the pine above Mergellina was arguably the most photographed tree on earth for a century, and the tree standing on that hillside now was planted in 1995 in place of the original. Six cities so far, eight trees.
